quests.instruction: You taste a tiny bit of the new food before taking a full bite. How do you feel?
quests.question: Cautious
quests.hint: Trying something small first before committing to more feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Trying something small first before committing to more gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: Tasting a small bite first is a smart, careful way to explore new foods!

quests.instruction: You practically bounce out of bed the morning of your favorite class. How do you feel?
quests.question: Enthusiastic
quests.hint: Waking up bursting with energy for something you love feels bright and eager.
quests.explanation: Waking up bursting with energy for something you love gives you a bright, eager feeling.
quests.funFact: Loving what you do is one of the biggest reasons mornings can feel exciting instead of slow!

quests.instruction: You borrowed your friend's book and it got a small tear. How do you feel?
quests.question: Guilty
quests.hint: Damaging something borrowed, even by accident, can weigh on your mind.
quests.explanation: Damaging something borrowed, even by accident, can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Telling a friend right away and offering to help fix it usually makes this feeling much lighter.

quests.instruction: You are the only one who does not know how to swim yet at the pool party. How do you feel?
quests.question: Insecure
quests.hint: Noticing you are behind others in a skill can make you doubt yourself a little.
quests.explanation: Noticing you are behind others in a skill can give you a small, self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Everyone learns skills like swimming at their own pace — there is no single right timeline!

quests.instruction: You have three big projects all due on the very same day. How do you feel?
quests.question: Overwhelmed
quests.hint: Having far too many things to handle all at once can make your mind feel full and jumbled.
quests.explanation: Having far too many things to handle all at once can give your mind a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Making a simple list and doing one task at a time can help this jumbled feeling untangle.

quests.instruction: You watch a chef flip a pancake high in the air and catch it perfectly. How do you feel?
quests.question: Amazed
quests.hint: Watching a tricky skill performed perfectly can leave you staring in wonder.
quests.explanation: Watching a tricky skill performed perfectly can leave you with a wide-eyed, astonished feeling.
quests.funFact: Chefs practice pancake flips hundreds of times before performing them so smoothly!

quests.instruction: You practice your multiplication facts every day until you know them by heart. How do you feel?
quests.question: Determined
quests.hint: Sticking to daily practice until something becomes easy feels strong and focused.
quests.explanation: Sticking to daily practice until something becomes easy gives you a strong, focused feeling.
quests.funFact: A few minutes of daily practice adds up to real mastery over just a few weeks!

quests.instruction: You keep asking how many more minutes until the movie starts. How do you feel?
quests.question: Impatient
quests.hint: Wanting something exciting to start sooner than it will feels restless.
quests.explanation: Wanting something exciting to start sooner than it will gives you a restless, waiting feeling.
quests.funFact: Previews before a movie are partly designed to help this restless waiting feeling pass!

quests.instruction: You finally spot your mom's car after waiting outside school in the cold. How do you feel?
quests.question: Relieved
quests.hint: Seeing a worry come to an end can make your whole body feel lighter.
quests.explanation: Seeing a worry come to an end, like spotting a ride you were waiting for, makes your body feel lighter.
quests.funFact: A warm car after waiting in the cold can make this lighter feeling even more comforting!

quests.instruction: You slow down your walking pace so your tired little cousin can keep up. How do you feel?
quests.question: Caring
quests.hint: Adjusting what you are doing to help someone smaller feels warm and kind.
quests.explanation: Adjusting what you are doing to help someone smaller feels warm and kind inside.
quests.funFact: Small adjustments like slowing down can make a big difference for someone who needs it!

quests.instruction: You check that the pool is deep enough before you dive in. How do you feel?
quests.question: Cautious
quests.hint: Checking for safety before jumping into something new feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Checking for safety before jumping into something new gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: Checking water depth before diving is an important safety step lifeguards always recommend!

quests.instruction: You wave your hand high, begging to go first in the relay race. How do you feel?
quests.question: Enthusiastic
quests.hint: Bursting with energy to be part of something right away feels bright and eager.
quests.explanation: Bursting with energy to be part of something right away gives you a bright, eager feeling.
quests.funFact: This bursting eagerness to go first is a great sign of team spirit and energy!

quests.instruction: You accidentally left your friend out of the game without meaning to. How do you feel?
quests.question: Guilty
quests.hint: Realizing someone felt left out because of something you did can weigh on your mind.
quests.explanation: Realizing someone felt left out because of something you did can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Inviting them to play next time is a simple, kind way to help make things feel right again.

quests.instruction: You are new to the team and unsure if you are as good as the others. How do you feel?
quests.question: Insecure
quests.hint: Comparing your skills to a team of people who have practiced longer can make you doubt yourself.
quests.explanation: Comparing your skills to teammates who have practiced longer can give you a self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Every teammate started out as a beginner once — skills grow the more you practice together!

quests.instruction: You are trying to clean an entire messy room by yourself in one afternoon. How do you feel?
quests.question: Overwhelmed
quests.hint: Facing a huge task all at once, with no clear starting point, can feel like too much at one time.
quests.explanation: Facing a huge task all at once, with no clear starting point, can give you a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Breaking a big mess into small sections, like one shelf at a time, makes it feel much more manageable!

quests.instruction: You see an enormous dinosaur skeleton for the first time at the museum. How do you feel?
quests.question: Amazed
quests.hint: Standing beneath something far bigger than you imagined can leave you staring in wonder.
quests.explanation: Standing beneath something far bigger than you imagined can leave you with an astonished feeling.
quests.funFact: Some dinosaur skeletons on display are longer than an entire school bus!

quests.instruction: You keep adjusting your paper airplane's wings until it finally flies straight. How do you feel?
quests.question: Determined
quests.hint: Trying small changes again and again until something finally works feels strong and focused.
quests.explanation: Trying small changes again and again until something finally works gives you a strong, focused feeling.
quests.funFact: Real engineers use this same trial-and-adjust method to design better and better flying machines!

quests.instruction: You keep peeking at the mailbox, waiting for your package to arrive. How do you feel?
quests.question: Impatient
quests.hint: Checking again and again for something you are eager to receive feels restless.
quests.explanation: Checking again and again for something you are eager to receive gives you a restless, waiting feeling.
quests.funFact: Tracking a package online can sometimes help this restless waiting feel a little more manageable!

quests.instruction: Your favorite toy is found completely unharmed after you thought you had lost it forever. How do you feel?
quests.question: Relieved
quests.hint: Getting back something you feared was gone for good can make your whole body feel lighter.
quests.explanation: Getting back something you feared was gone for good makes your whole body feel lighter and calmer.
quests.funFact: Checking under furniture is often where 'lost forever' toys are actually hiding!

quests.instruction: You offer your extra blanket to a friend who says they feel cold. How do you feel?
quests.question: Caring
quests.hint: Giving up something of your own to help someone feel more comfortable feels warm and kind.
quests.explanation: Giving up something of your own to help someone feel more comfortable gives you a warm, kind feeling.
quests.funFact: Small acts of comfort like sharing a blanket are simple ways friends take care of each other!

quests.instruction: You slow down and look carefully before petting a dog you do not know. How do you feel?
quests.question: Cautious
quests.hint: Taking a moment to observe before approaching something unfamiliar feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Taking a moment to observe before approaching something unfamiliar gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking an owner first is always the safest way to greet a dog you have not met before!

quests.instruction: You talk nonstop about the science fair project you cannot wait to build. How do you feel?
quests.question: Enthusiastic
quests.hint: Overflowing with excitement about an idea can make you want to tell everyone about it.
quests.explanation: Overflowing with excitement about an idea makes you want to tell everyone, giving you an eager feeling.
quests.funFact: This bursting, talkative excitement is often the spark behind some of the best creative projects!

quests.instruction: You ate the last cookie that your brother was saving without asking. How do you feel?
quests.question: Guilty
quests.hint: Taking something you knew belonged to someone else can weigh on your mind afterward.
quests.explanation: Taking something you knew belonged to someone else can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Offering to replace what you took is a simple way to help make things right again.

quests.instruction: You wonder if your drawing is good enough to show the class. How do you feel?
quests.question: Insecure
quests.hint: Comparing your own work to others before sharing it can make you doubt yourself.
quests.explanation: Comparing your own work to others before sharing it can give you a small, self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Every artist's style looks different — that difference is exactly what makes art interesting!

quests.instruction: The store is so loud and crowded that you cannot think straight. How do you feel?
quests.question: Overwhelmed
quests.hint: Too much noise and too many people at once can make your mind feel full and jumbled.
quests.explanation: Too much noise and too many people at once can give your mind a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Stepping outside for a moment of quiet can help a busy, jumbled feeling settle down.

quests.instruction: You test the ice with your foot before stepping onto the frozen pond. How do you feel?
quests.question: Cautious
quests.hint: Checking carefully for safety before doing something new feels careful and watchful.
quests.explanation: Checking carefully for safety before doing something new gives you a careful, watchful feeling.
quests.funFact: Testing ice carefully before stepping on it is exactly what safety experts recommend!

quests.instruction: You cannot stop talking about the new hobby you just started. How do you feel?
quests.question: Enthusiastic
quests.hint: Wanting to share every detail about something new you love feels bright and eager.
quests.explanation: Wanting to share every detail about something new you love gives you a bright, eager feeling.
quests.funFact: This bursting eagerness to share is one of the best parts of discovering a new hobby!

quests.instruction: You accidentally broke your friend's toy and have not told them yet. How do you feel?
quests.question: Guilty
quests.hint: Knowing you did something wrong and have not made it right yet can weigh on your mind.
quests.explanation: Knowing you did something wrong and have not made it right yet can give you a heavy, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Telling the truth quickly, even about an accident, usually helps this heavy feeling lift fast.

quests.instruction: You are the slowest reader in your reading group and worry others will notice. How do you feel?
quests.question: Insecure
quests.hint: Comparing your pace to others in a group can make you doubt yourself a little.
quests.explanation: Comparing your pace to others in a group can give you a small, self-doubting feeling.
quests.funFact: Readers all grow at their own speed — steady practice helps everyone improve over time!

quests.instruction: You are asked to remember a very long list of instructions all at once. How do you feel?
quests.question: Overwhelmed
quests.hint: Too much information coming at once can make your mind feel full and jumbled.
quests.explanation: Too much information coming at once can give your mind a full, jumbled feeling.
quests.funFact: Writing instructions down step by step can help a jumbled mind keep track more easily!
